changes: Fixed: on Android, Back on the Budget tab sometimes closed the app without asking. It now always says "Press back again to exit" first

Fixed: on Android, Back could close the app from Settings (for example Settings › General › Back). Back now walks back through the screens you opened, one at a time, and never adds history of its own, which Android treated as a reason to leave the app

Back goes up one screen at a time instead of always to the Budget tab: Settings › Sync & server › Back is Settings, then Budget; an account › Back is Accounts, then Budget. Pop-ups still close first, and the ‹ buttons on screens work the same way
Budget tab: large amounts ($10,000 and up) no longer run into each other; the columns grow to fit and big numbers are drawn a little smaller
Choosing a category is a compact list, one line per category with what's left on the right, so a long list is quicker to scan
A purchase whose tip hasn't posted shows "+ tip waiting" under its amount instead of a label that got cut off

Fixed: people shared at "Add purchases" could pay cards, make transfers and add income. They now add and change their own purchases only: Pay card and Transfer are hidden for them, Quick add offers just Spent, and the server refuses anything else

Tap-to-pay purchases waiting to be logged are shared with the budget: every phone and the web app show the same "Log tap-to-pay purchase" bubble ("caught on another phone" when it was), and saving or dismissing it on any device clears it everywhere. Nothing touches the budget until it's saved
A purchase saved on two devices at once is still one transaction
Covers link both ways: a category covered from another says "Covered $X from Emergency Fund ›", and the one that gave says "Gave $X to Dining Out ›". Tap the name to go to that category
In the Owed to / Paying back sheet, tap a category to go straight to it
Money taken from next month now shows on the Budget tab until it's repaid: "↪ Owed to December" in the month that borrowed and "↩ Paying back November" in the next, with what it covered and when
Tap it for the details: how much is still owed, how much money coming in has already paid back (oldest first), and Undo for each one. The covered category says so too

Bank check (tap Ready to assign): money taken from next month is its own line, and a leftover one that no longer covers anything is flagged as "Something doesn't add up" with a button to clear it, instead of saying everything matches. The money check on the Budget tab lists it too

Fixed: money taken from next month to cover overspending kept counting after you deleted the purchases or lowered the category, adding money that didn't exist to Ready to Assign. A borrow now only counts as far as it's still needed: it never lifts Ready to Assign above $0, and next month is charged only that much

Fixed (server): a second budget on the same server couldn't keep settings whose names another budget already used, such as badges, the card payoff category, card rolling, closed months and the debt plan. They were refused and lost, so badges kept being awarded again. Each budget now keeps its own settings; existing servers are upgraded on start
Badges are awarded once and kept. New monthly badges (Every dollar placed, Targets funded, Five quiet days, Kept the log, Clean finish) can each be earned once a month and start over on the 1st

Every drop-down list in the app (account and category pickers, how often, goal type, report filters, sharing levels, settings and more) now opens in the app's own style, light or dark, instead of Android's plain system popup
Quick add: choosing the account (and the From / To accounts of a transfer or card payment) opens a list in the app's own style, light or dark, instead of Android's plain system popup

New server: after you create the password, setup walks you through your accounts, paycheck, bills and everyday amounts, and ends with Connect your phone (show the pairing code, or Not now), instead of dropping you on the pairing page
Fixed: card payments are counted in date order. A payment pays the card's debt that existed when you made it, so purchases made after it stay Ready to pay instead of moving into Ready to Assign

Card payoff: the payoff category now shows the card debt it still holds. A payment to a card first uses its Ready to pay, then pays that debt down and comes out of Ready to Assign by itself, so there's no need to assign money to record a payment (and nothing can count twice)
Money assigned to the payoff category is set aside for your next payment, shown as Ready to pay on the cards in your order or your debt plan's
Accounts › Ready to pay: tap a card to see where its money comes from
Fixed: 1.51.1 counted payoff-category money that had already paid a card down again, so another card's Ready to pay could ask you to pay it twice. Money that already went to a card is used up
Each card's page shows where its Ready to pay comes from: your payoff category, this month's purchases by category, and earlier purchases

Card payoff with 'Pay cards in my debt plan's order' off: you set the order cards get the money in (▲ ▼ under Budget rules), and it all goes to the first card until it's covered, instead of being split across every card
Cover sheet: when Ready to assign can cover it, that's the only choice shown
Each category shows how this month's spending was paid: on credit cards (card by card) versus cash or debit
Cover sheet: when part of the overspending is on a credit card, cover all of it or only the cash part. The card part waits on the card and, with rolling on, moves to your payoff category at month end

Card payoff: money assigned to the payoff category now pays cards in your debt plan's order (minimums first, then snowball or avalanche) instead of by balance, and rolled overspending is counted on the card it was spent on. Switch it off under Budget rules › Credit card overspending to give each card back what was rolled from it

Server: starts even when its data folder was created owned by root (as Unraid and Docker do): it makes the folder belong to PUID:PGID (Unraid template 99:100, otherwise 1000:1000), then runs as that user
Unraid: the template is installed with one terminal command until it's in Community Applications (DOCKER.md)

Cover overspending from wherever there's money: tap Cover and pick Ready to assign or a category that can spare it (categories keep what their target and this month's bills still need). A source without enough covers what it can and the rest stays to cover
When nothing can cover it, Take from next month's money: the category goes back to $0 now and the amount comes off next month's Ready to assign, shown under Ready to assign in both months
The month-end "ended overspent" notice offers Take from this month's money or Other ways; Cover all in the money check and month review use the same choices

Budget table on a phone: pick Assigned, Spent or Available and see four months side by side with no sideways scrolling, newest on the right. Tap a number to change what's assigned that month, with one-tap Same as last month, Target and What was spent
The Tiles view on the Budget tab is gone; categories are always the list
Reports on a computer: the cards pack together without big gaps, and ✎ Customize lets you move, resize, remove and add back each report, or pick a layout (Overview, Trends first, Spending focus)
Your Reports layout is remembered on each device, like the Budget dashboard's
On a computer every page has the same width as the Budget dashboard, so nothing jumps around when you switch tabs
Reports: the custom report's dates, account, category and grouping now sit in the same box as its result, with the net total at the top
On a computer, the Budget table fills the window so several months fit side by side
Wide screens use their space: no empty strip down the right, Badges and the forecast lay out side by side, and an account's transactions show the category in its own column
Once Budget is open source under the GNU AGPL v3; About says so and links to the code
Budget is now called Once Budget, with a new icon (also the themed icon on Android 13+, the notification icon, and the icon when you add it to a home screen from a browser)
Nothing about your budget changes: same data, same server, same settings

Fixed: after a budget was restored from a server backup (or erased), other phones and browsers could keep things the server no longer had, such as an old test account. They now download the budget again on their next sync
Every device downloads its budget fresh once after this update, which clears out anything left over from before
Smoother scrolling: the app now uses your phone's fastest refresh rate (120 Hz where available), and pages scroll the way the rest of the phone does
Long account histories load as you scroll instead of all at once
Saving is quicker, and background syncs with nothing new no longer redraw the app (a small stutter about once a minute)
Large JSON imports take seconds instead of minutes

Signing in at home without the server password: opened through Cloudflare, Settings › Sync & server › Get a code to sign in at home shows a one-time code for the home address's sign-in page (Sign in with a code), as the same person with the same budgets
Every transaction records when it was entered (tap-to-pay: the moment you paid), and accounts keep that order
Uncleared transactions stay at the top; once cleared, a transaction moves into its place by date and time. Editing never moves it
Newest shows everything by date and time; editing a transaction shows when it was entered, and tapping someone's initials shows when they entered it
Tap the initials on a transaction to see who entered it. They now show the person's name, including people added on your server's Pair a phone page
Colours: each person in a shared budget has a colour for their initials. Tap their circle in Who can open this budget to change it (owners for anyone, everyone for themselves)
Sharing levels: when you share a budget, pick Change everything, Add purchases (adds purchases and changes only their own) or View only, and change it any time
Your server enforces the level on every change; someone with a limited level sees a note at the top saying what they can do, and View only has no + button
Fixed: Pair a phone, after adding a person or showing someone's code, could show the budget instead of the page
Rename and Delete are only offered for budgets you own
Share with no longer lists old built-in sign-in names from a test mode (such as me@home) that nobody can sign in as. They still show under Who can open this budget, so you can remove them
Fixed: scanning the Pair a phone QR code with the camera gave a web search. The code is now a normal link to a page on your server with Open in Budget (and the code to type)

The QR code points at your server's home address even when Pair a phone is opened through Cloudflare, because a new phone can't pair through Cloudflare. The home address is remembered, or typed on that page
Connected through Cloudflare and added your home address? Save & test now pairs the phone with it by itself (through Cloudflare), so home no longer says Refused
Pair again with a code is always offered while connected
Settings › Sync & server › Server password: create your server's password from the app, or change it later
Forgot it? Signed in through Cloudflare as the admin, you can set a new one without the old one
Fixed: once the web app had been opened in a browser, the server's own pages (password setup, sign-in, Pair a phone) showed the budget instead

Fixed: switching a Cloudflare server to password mode, the password couldn't be created unless you were the very first person who ever used the server. Anyone who already owned its main budget can create it through Cloudflare, and becomes the admin
Fixed: until the password was created, the web app through Cloudflare kept bouncing to the password page, so its update banner never cleared

Home and Cloudflare together: a server with AUTH_MODE=password that keeps its Cloudflare settings accepts Cloudflare sign-ins away and the password and paired phones at home, as the same person with the same budgets
A phone already connected through Cloudflare can Pair with a code to sync at home too, without changing anything else
On a server that already has budgets, the password can only be created through Cloudflare, signed in as the admin, so nobody else on the network can claim it
🔒 Budgets on a shared server are private: each budget belongs to the people in it, and nobody else on the server can open it or see that it exists

Settings › Sync & server › Who can open this budget lists them. Owners share a budget (by email with Cloudflare, or by picking a person with a server password), make someone an owner, or stop sharing; anyone can leave a budget someone else owns
Server password (home network): the admin adds people on Pair a phone, and each gets a one-time code for their phone or browser, so they never need the server password
Only owners can rename, delete, erase or restore a budget. In open or local mode everyone still shares every budget, and the app says so
Servers set up before keep working as they were: everyone who had signed in owns every existing budget
💵 When do you get paid: set your pay schedule on the Forecast (weekly, every 2 weeks, twice a month or monthly) and one payday to count from. No amount needed
The forecast checks each account until your real next payday, and paydays show in the list, on the chart and as a green ring on the calendar
Paydays on a weekend move to the Friday before (or Monday after, or stay). Two people on different schedules can each add one
The menu fits on the screen: its items sit in two columns, so About and Close no longer need scrolling
Money in your budget has two tabs, Bank check and Hold for next month, so each fits without scrolling. The Hold button in the header opens the Hold tab
(i) pop-ups and What's new use the whole screen height before anything scrolls, and their buttons always stay in view
The add and edit screen fits on a small screen: the number pad and Save or Update are always visible without scrolling
The tip choices sit on one line, and the account and date share a row
Editing a tipped purchase shows the tip percent you picked instead of Other
Messages at the bottom of the screen use the full width instead of wrapping into a narrow column

💵 Tips: every tap-to-pay prompt has a Tip row (No tip, 15%, 18%, 20%, Other) with the total. Your budget counts the full amount straight away; typed purchases have + tip too, and a purchase saved from the notification offers + Tip in the message that follows
Until your bank posts the tip, the purchase shows tip pending and the account says what your bank shows for now. The bank check and Reconcile mention it too
When the bank catches up, tap the circle on the purchase: Yes clears it, or type the amount the bank shows and the purchase and its category update
Tips still not posted after 10 days are listed in Money check
Server: transactions remember a pending tip (update the server so tips stay marked as pending when they sync)
Reports › Where it went: choose which categories the spending chart shows (🎯 Categories), so a big debt payment doesn't fill the chart while you pay it down
Hide from chart in a slice's pop-up, a one-tap Hide for your card payoff category, and a Not shown line under the chart with Show all
New (i) help buttons across the app: tap one next to a heading for a short pop-up on how it works

Covered: Ready to assign, the category columns, Money check, Needs, Over plan, Bank check, Age of money, Net worth, Ready to pay, Where it went, the Reports charts, Forecast, Scheduled, Streaks, the debt planner, and the Settings for your server, automatic backups, tap-to-pay, card overspending and closing months
Debt planner: debts are numbered in payoff order, and the one getting the extra money now is marked in green
Debt planner: when snowball and avalanche give the same plan (your smallest debt also has the highest rate), it now says so instead of looking like nothing happened
New (i) buttons on the debt planner open a short explanation of snowball, avalanche, the extra amount and the payoff order
Fixed: tapping Connect in Settings › Sync & server on the phone showed an error ("Converting circular structure to JSON") instead of connecting

📱 Pair a phone with a QR code: servers can now have their own password (AUTH_MODE=password). Open the server in a browser, create the password, then Pair a phone shows a QR code. Scan it with your phone's camera and Budget connects, with no addresses to type (or use Pair with a code in Settings › Sync & server)
Each phone and browser gets its own key, listed on the server's Pair a phone page where you can remove one
The server is now ready to publish as an image for PCs, NAS boxes and Raspberry Pi, with an Unraid template and a step-by-step install guide
Examples in tips, the changelog and the user manual use made-up store names and card numbers

📊 Reports › Where it went: a donut chart of your spending by category or group for this month, last month, 3 months or this year. Tap a slice to see its transactions, and a transaction to edit it. Card payments and money moved into the card payoff category don't count as spending
Over plan folds to one line until you tap it, and each category in it opens that category
Fixed: on a foldable phone (unfolded) or a wide screen, pop-ups opened from a category, like Schedule as a monthly bill, only dimmed the screen. Every pop-up now shows on top
The + button hides while a pop-up is open
⌨️ Type amounts with a computer keyboard in Quick add: the number pad always types the amount (even from the Payee box), Backspace deletes a digit, Enter saves
Debt payoff planner: the rate and minimum boxes no longer jump while you type; they save when you leave the box
Scheduled: the form says what's missing instead of silently not saving, and asks before discarding what you typed
A category with a monthly target can be scheduled as a monthly bill in one tap from its panel
New credit cards and loans ask for the interest rate, minimum payment and due day: the planner gets the numbers, and the monthly payment is scheduled with a reminder

Money in your budget now checks against your bank only: Ready to Assign + In categories + held + money set aside to pay cards should equal your checking, savings and cash accounts, with a ✓ when it does
Cards and loans have their own Debts section, showing what you owe and how much of each card is ready to pay

💰 Tap Ready to Assign for Money in your budget: each account's balance and the total to compare with your bank, and where the money is (in categories without overspending taken off, Ready to Assign, held, overspent), with a ✓ when it all adds up. Hold for next month is here too, and the Held card at the bottom of the budget is gone
Needs no longer lists the card payoff category, since that money is spent down rather than filled up
Reports: choose which accounts the reports include (🏦 Accounts)
Debt payoff planner: Leave out of plan on any debt (for example a mortgage), with Add back
Long category names no longer cut off their ✓ or ▲ badge
Fixed: the first letter you typed in a field like Payee was hidden under the focus outline. The whole field now lights up green while you type in it
The over-plan amount is shown in red
Fixed: text was cut off at the left edge of a highlighted row: the selected category (on wide screens with the side panel) and selected transactions in an account
The + button steps aside while transactions are selected, so it doesn't sit behind the selection bar
▲ Over plan: categories that spent more than their monthly target get an orange marker, even after you cover it, so you can see what needs a bigger target

Over plan card: lists those categories, plus scheduled bills that recently charged more than planned ("Netflix charged $22.99, scheduled $16.99") with an Update button that also raises the category's target

The + button: bottom-right corner of the window on computers (pages keep a margin so it never covers a card); on phones it slides away while you scroll down and comes back when you scroll up; hidden on Settings, Badges, History and Setup

The top of the Budget screen is much shorter: Payday check is one line (red if an account will dip below zero), streaks, savings goals and badges are a row of small chips, and Income is one line you can tap to open
Savings goal jars moved to Menu › Badges & goals; tap a goal's chip on the Budget screen for how it's doing
✏️ Rename categories: open a category and change its Name. It keeps its money, transactions, target and payee rules, and Undo puts the old name back
Rename groups too: tap ✎ next to a group's name in Groups view
Tiles: category names wrap onto two lines before being shortened, and can no longer run into the next tile. Rings line up along each row

Fixed: a category with a monthly target counted as underfunded again once you spent from it. It's now funded once you've assigned its target this month (or already have that much in it), so spending doesn't put it back in Needs or Fill to targets
Needs shows how much you've assigned toward a monthly target
Save-by-date goals: this month's share no longer shrinks as you assign it, so it shows as done once you've put in the month's amount

🎆 Your year: the recap for a whole year (Reports › Your 2026, or from the bottom of a monthly recap): what you kept, a bar for each month, where it went, your best month, biggest purchase, regular spot, no-spend days, months on budget, debt paid down and badges earned. Save as PDF
Recaps no longer count the starting balances of new accounts as income
Updated user manual: getting started, icons, streaks, badges, goal jars and your year, with new screenshots
🔥 Streaks on the Budget screen: days in a row with something logged, months in a row with nothing overspent, and no-spend days this month
🏅 Badges (Menu › Badges & streaks): 13 to earn, from your first transaction to debt-free. Each is celebrated once when you earn it; ones you'd already earned are awarded quietly
🐷 Savings goals: save-by-date goals get a jar that fills up, and a note saying whether you're on track and when you'll get there at your current pace. Reaching one gets a proper celebration

👋 Guided setup for a new budget: add your accounts and balances, your paycheck, your monthly bills (each becomes a scheduled bill with a target) and rough amounts for everyday spending. Every step can be skipped; rerun it from Settings › General

🛒 Category icons: every category gets an icon suggested from its name (🛒 Groceries, 🏠 Rent, ⛽ Gas…), shown in the budget, tiles, the category picker, Needs, Quick add and the recap. Change it or turn it off from the category's panel › Icon. Names that already start with an emoji are left as they are
↻ Pull down at the top of Budget or Accounts to sync right away
Fixed: syncing failed with "Server answered 500" after removing a category's target from the Needs list. The change that was stuck is sent correctly now and nothing is lost
The server also no longer lets one unexpected value stop the whole sync
Choosing the account for new transactions (Settings › General) no longer reloads the page, so the browser's own "Leave site?" box can't appear; a short note confirms it instead
Restoring a backup, resetting, connecting a server or switching budget no longer show that browser box either; they already ask in Budget's own pop-up first
Needs: tap a category to change its target amount, switch between each month and by a date, or remove the target, right in the list
🎯 Needs: a new choice next to Remaining and Spent that lists only categories below their target, biggest shortfall first. An amber badge on it shows how many there are
Each one has a + button that funds just that category to its target (or as much as Ready to Assign has), without opening it
"All groups" is now "Groups" so all four choices fit on a phone

Fixed: Quick add no longer asks "Is this a payment to (your loan)?" just because the category has "car", "auto" or "house" in its name (Car Registration, Daycare…). It asks only when the category is one you've mostly paid that loan from, or is plainly a loan category (Car loan, Mortgage, Car payment)
Answering "No, it's spending" is remembered for that category, so it doesn't ask again

Computers and tablets: Accounts, Reports, the debt planner and Settings pages use the full width with cards side by side; Settings shows its list on the left and the page on the right; an account's transactions, Scheduled, History and the payday forecast get a wider column
The + button and bottom bar line up with the page at every width
A new screen now opens at its top, instead of where the last screen was scrolled to
Accounts are listed in the order you arranged them everywhere, so the first account is always the one new transactions start in (unless you chose a default)
Importing a backup as a copy keeps each debt's interest rate and minimum, and your card payoff category
On/off switches in Settings sit beside their labels again
Updated user manual with new screenshots
Behind-the-scenes tidy-up
🧹 Settings is now a short list: General, Privacy & security, Notifications, Budget rules, Sync & server, Backups & data. Each opens its own page, and ‹ at the top goes back to the list
History has its own screen (Menu › History). Version, updates and what's new are under Settings › About
Removed the Scheduled card (it's in the Menu and the forecast calendar) and folded the offline and tap-to-pay explanations into one line each

🎨 New category picker: tapping Category opens a full-height grid of tiles grouped like your budget, each showing what's left (green, amber at $0, red when overspent). No keyboard unless you tap Search
Suggested tiles come first: the payee's usual category and the ones you use most
The same picker is used everywhere you choose a category: Quick add, splits, loan payments, Scheduled, CSV import and Settings

✨ Monthly recap (Menu › Monthly recap, Reports, or ✨ Recap in Month review): your month as a short story. What you kept and what share of income that was, money in and out, net worth change, where it went with changes from the month before, the biggest swings, and highlights (biggest purchase, your regular spot, no-spend days, biggest spending day, categories that stayed within budget, debt paid down)
Save as PDF to keep or share it
Calendar: + Recurring on any day adds a bill, paycheck or transfer starting that day

📅 Bills calendar: Payday forecast now has List and Calendar views. The calendar shows every scheduled bill (card bills too), paycheck and transfer as coloured dots, and shades the days an account would be below zero
Tap a day to see what's due, with Post, Skip or Move to another date, plus each account's balance at the end of that day. Look up to 12 months ahead

⛰ Debt payoff planner (Menu › Debt payoff planner): your credit cards and loans with each one's interest rate and minimum, an extra amount per month, and Snowball (smallest first) or Avalanche (highest interest first)
Shows your debt-free month, total interest, how much sooner and cheaper it is than paying minimums only, what the other order would cost, a chart, and what to pay on each debt this month
Rates and minimums are estimated until you enter yours, and saved with the budget (synced to your server if connected). Also a Debt payoff dashboard widget

Automatic phone backups are now optional for budgets synced with a server (the server already keeps 14 days): Settings › Automatic backups › Also back up on this phone. Offline budgets stay on by default

💾 Automatic backups on your phone: a copy of each budget every day you use it (when you open Budget, and when you leave it if anything changed). The same day's copy is overwritten, and the last 14 are kept
Settings › Automatic backups: Back up now, and Restore from any of the 14. A restore puts the budget back exactly as it was that day, and Undo reverses it
Also copy to a folder: choose a folder Google Drive syncs, or an SD card, so a copy lives off the phone (Android's folder picker, no permission). It also keeps 14
Server: one backup per night (taken as soon as it can if the server was off at 3 a.m.), the last 14 days kept

🏠 Home-screen widget: Ready to Assign, your three lowest categories, a payday warning if an account will dip below zero, and a + button that opens Quick add. Add it from Settings › Privacy › Add Budget to your home screen, or from your launcher's widget list
The widget shows •••• instead of amounts while Hide balances or App lock is on
It updates whenever your numbers change in the app, and uses no extra permission

📈 Payday forecast (Menu › Payday forecast): each checking, savings and cash account's balance projected from your scheduled bills, paychecks and transfers, with a chart and a running balance for every item. Choose 2 weeks, 5 weeks or 3 months

A Payday check card on the Budget screen warns when an account would go below zero before payday ("Chequing goes to −$452.80 on Nov 9 (Rent). Payday is Nov 13"), or confirms it stays above its lowest point
Also available as a dashboard widget on wide screens

⚡ One-tap logging: a tap-to-pay notification now offers "Save as Dining Out" (or whichever category fits) without opening the app. Budget picks it from your payee rules, then your past purchases at that store
"Other…" opens Quick add to choose something else, and Dismiss still drops it
Saved purchases are written at once if Budget is running, otherwise the next time you open it, with a note and Undo
The store-to-category list stays on your phone, inside the app
Back goes straight to the Budget screen from anywhere, instead of stepping through every screen you visited; Back on Budget then asks to exit. Open pop-ups still close first
With App lock on, tapping a tap-to-pay notification always asks for your fingerprint first, then opens the purchase
👁 Hide balances: the eye button at the top (or Settings › Privacy) blurs every amount; press and hold an amount to peek. Remembered on each device, in the app and the browser

🔒 App lock (Android app): Settings › Privacy › Lock with your phone's screen lock. Uses your fingerprint, face or PIN, with no extra permission. Lock when leaving, or after 1 or 5 minutes away; the recent-apps preview is hidden while it's on
Returning from Budget's own screens (file picker, Wallet, sign-in) never locks it
The menu slides up from the bottom and back down when it closes; swipe up on the bottom bar to open it, drag it down to close
Sheets slide up and pop-ups fade in (skipped when your phone's "remove animations" setting is on)
🎉 Confetti when Ready to Assign reaches exactly $0: every dollar has a job
💳 Celebrations for wins: a card paid off, a category reaching its target, age of money passing 30 days
Envelopes fill: assigning money pours into the category's bar or ring
Clearing a transaction pops its check with a little buzz
A category that just went over budget gives a short shake so you notice
Friendlier empty screens
All motion is skipped when your phone's "remove animations" setting is on

Wide screens (unfolded phones, tablets, computers): the Budget tab becomes a dashboard you can arrange. Tap ✎ Customize to pick a layout (Three panes, Budget + detail, Wide table), drag widgets by ⠿, make them wider or narrower, remove them or add more
Widgets: Budget, Category detail, Accounts, Net worth, Spending, Due soon, Ready to pay, Reports and Budget table
Each screen size remembers its own layout, so the unfolded phone and a computer can differ; folded phones keep the normal layout
Money rolls to its new value with a green or red glow: Ready to Assign, net worth, account balances and categories
Imports come alive again: rows land in batches with a progress bar and running total (still one Undo, still can't run twice)
Animations are skipped when your phone's "remove animations" setting is on
Fixed: some phones greyed out bank CSV files in the file picker (they label CSVs "text/comma-separated-values"); every common CSV and JSON label is accepted now
CSV import uses your bank's own transaction reference when the file has one, so duplicates are matched exactly (two identical purchases on one day both import)
The import screen explains that every bank's file differs, which duplicate check it's using, and that the whole import is one Undo
Choose a budget: Put on your server (checks the server can be reached, creates a budget with the same name and uploads it) and Make offline
Connecting a budget from Settings always lets you choose the server budget, including a new one, so a second budget is never merged into your main one
Fixed: tapping Import more than once during a CSV import could import the whole file again (seen with a 402-row bank file imported twice)
CSV import is much faster: 402 rows now take under a second instead of about 40 on a phone, and stay one Undo
CSV import no longer mistakes a "CREDIT/DEBIT" column for amounts
Tap-to-pay with several budgets: choose which budget purchases go to (Settings → Tap-to-pay capture); only that budget shows them, and tapping a prompt opens it there
New (optional): roll credit card overspending into a payoff category at month end, so categories start each month clean and card debt sits in one place (Settings → Credit card overspending)
Only the card share rolls: overspending paid with cash or debit stays red in its category
Card payoff shows in Money check as "Card debt to fund" with a Fund button, is included in Fill to targets, and each roll is listed in Month review with Undo
A card's starting balance can go straight into the payoff category from the card's Ready to pay panel
